title: Remote and hybrid work
body:
Remote work was once seen as a perk offered by a handful of technology firms. Over the past few years it has become a standard option in many industries. Supporters argue that it saves commuting time and widens the pool of people a company can hire, since location matters less.

Critics point out that new employees, in particular, learn faster when they can watch experienced colleagues at work, and that informal conversations, which often spark ideas, are harder to arrange online.

Many organisations have therefore settled on a hybrid model, asking staff to come in on a few fixed days so that collaboration and mentoring happen in person while focused work is done from home.
